summary: Roland Harweg was a linguist who studied under Alfred Schmitt (~1954–1960) and Peter Hartmann (~1957–1962). He held academic posts at the University of Münster (~1964–1969) and Ruhr University Bochum (~1969–1999).
Roland Knyvet Wilson was an Indologist who earned his B.A. at the University of Cambridge (~1859–1863). He later served at Cambridge as Reader in Indian Law from 1884 to 1893.
Roland Steiner is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who studied under Michael Hahn (attested 1990). He held a post as Assistant Professor Dr. at the University of Marburg (attested 2002).

Roland Wenzlhuemer is a historian who earned his doctorate at the University of Salzburg (1999–2002) and completed his habilitation at Heidelberg University (~2008–2011). He held positions at Heidelberg, Basel, and the University of Munich, where he became director in 2021.

Rolf Alfred Stein specialized in Tibetology and Sinology, studying under scholars including Marcelle Lalou, Jacques Bacot, and Marcel Granet. He held major posts at EFEO, EPHE (1951–1975), and the Collège de France (1965–1982).

Rolf Hiersche was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Richard Karl Heinrich von Kienle and earned a Ph.D. at the University of Jena (1945–1951). His career included posts at Humboldt University, FU Berlin, Lille, and Giessen (1970–1989).

Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (2010–2016) under Helmut Tauscher. He held positions at Vienna, Leipzig, Erlangen-Nuremberg, Heidelberg University, and the University of Munich.

Romain Rolland was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, Lycée Saint-Louis, École Normale Supérieure, and the University of Paris. He held academic posts at École Normale Supérieure and the University of Paris (~1903–1912).

Roman Ghirshman was an archaeologist and specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied in Paris. He directed the Musée du Louvre (1931–1972) and served as acting director of the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan (1941–1943).

Roman Jakobson was a linguist who studied at Moscow University under Wiktor Jan Porzeziński and at the German University of Prague. He held academic posts at Masaryk University (~1933–1939), Harvard University (~1949–1967), and MIT (~1957–1967).

Romila Thapar is a historian and Indologist who studied at Panjab University and earned her doctorate under Arthur Llewellyn Basham at SOAS. She held major posts at Kurukshetra University, the University of Delhi, and Jawaharlal Nehru University (1970–1991).
Ron Garry is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer was a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields who studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and under traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche from around 1978 to 2017.

Ronald D. Schwartz is a scholar in Tibetology and sociology who served as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland (attested 1998) and as an Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.

Ronald E. Purser is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and management who studied under Koshin Ogui in 1985. He held faculty posts at Loyola University Chicago (~1989–1995) and San Francisco State University (~1995).

Ronald Egan is a Sinologist who completed his Ph.D. at Harvard University (~1971–1977). He held academic posts at Harvard, Wellesley College, the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1992–2012), and Stanford University (~2012–2023).

Ronald Eric Emmerick was a scholar of Iranian, Indological, and Tibetan studies who earned degrees at Sydney, Oxford, and Cambridge, studying under Harold Walter Bailey. He held posts at SOAS (1967–1971) and the University of Hamburg (1971–2001).
Ronald Herman Poelmeijer was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1966–1975). He served as Lecturer of Tibetan at Leiden University from ~1978 until 1993.
Ronald Inden is an Indologist and historian who served at the University of Chicago, where he became Professor Emeritus of History and South Asian Languages and Civilizations (attested 2007, 2026).

Ronald M. Davidson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who earned his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley (-1985) under multiple teachers. He held posts as a professor at California State University, Northridge, and at Fairfield University.
